Call of Duty. An annual first-person shooter franchise that launched from Activision in 2003, it has dominated console gaming and esports for two decades by pioneering a formula of cinematic campaigns, large-scale multiplayer maps, and unlockable progression systems. The series debuted in 2003 on PC, but Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare in 2007 revolutionized everything by abandoning World War II settings for contemporary geopolitics. It introduced the iconic Captain Roach and the SAS operator Captain Price as the franchise's most recognizable soldiers. The games established an annual release cycle and a premium multiplayer model built around fast-paced deathmatch, team modes like Capture the Flag and Search and Destroy, and progression-based unlocks for weapons, attachments, and cosmetics.

The franchise eventually split into two alternating sub-franchises. Modern Warfare covers contemporary and near-future conflicts, while Black Ops focuses on covert Cold War operations and fictional missions, each with its own distinct tone and cast of characters. Multiplayer map design emphasizes three-lane symmetry to keep team play balanced, and killstreaks—reward chains for consecutive kills—let players call in airstrikes or helicopters, turning an individual's performance into a team advantage. Call of Duty: Black Ops introduced Zombie mode in 2010, a cooperative wave of undead enemies that spawned its own competitive community and lore spanning multiple entries. The franchise reached its peaks with Modern Warfare 2 in 2009, which became a cultural phenomenon, and Black Ops in 2010. More recently, entries have had to compete with Valorant, CS:GO, and Overwatch for both esports and casual audiences. Warzone, the free-to-play battle royale launched in 2020, brought the franchise into the live-service model, though later entries have struggled with integration and player retention. Activision publishes and primarily develops the series alongside Infinity Ward, Treyarch, and Sledgehammer Games, establishing a dominant presence as the leading FPS franchise of the 2000s and 2010s and supporting the Call of Duty League professional esports circuit.
